# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꖜ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The previous call was rejected because the engraved mark cannot be included literally in spoken text. I will refer to it descriptively and ask Mute to use Deaf’s visual reading of the bomb together with the manual.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I can reach the bomb. The plate has an engraved mark that I cannot pronounce or identify by sight. I cannot identify the display, light, colours, or wire markings. Please consult the manual and obtain Deaf's description of the engraved mark and visual details, then tell me which wire position to cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꖜ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb display is 0. Light is off. Plate is engraved with a question mark. Wires in order are yellow, green, red. Mute signalled three gestures to Deaf: index finger up, victory sign, rock-on.

I know the bomb’s visible facts through Deaf: display 0, light off, a question-mark engraving, and wires ordered yellow, green, red. I still do not know the manual’s rule or which wire is safe. Mute’s gestures to Deaf are not available to me, so I will ask Mute directly for the required cut position.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports: display 0, light off, question-mark engraving, and wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. What does the manual require? Tell me the exact wire position to cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꖜ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's latest five gestures, in order: index finger up; victory sign; rock-on; pointing at you; pointing down.

Deaf has relayed five gestures from Mute, but only their descriptions are available to me; they do not yet establish an unambiguous wire position or manual instruction. I will ask Mute to state the required position plainly rather than rely on gesture encoding.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please state plainly which wire position the manual requires me to cut. Do not encode the answer only with gestures.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꖜ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's latest gesture is thumbs down.

The thumbs-down gesture does not identify a wire position. The earlier gestures may be an attempted code, but no reliable mapping from them to positions 1–3 has been established. Since Mute cannot speak, I will explicitly ask for a gesture encoding that uses one distinct gesture for the required wire and have Deaf relay it.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I still need the exact wire position. Please send exactly one gesture meaning wire 1, wire 2, or wire 3; Deaf can relay its description.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꖜ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's latest gestures, in order: thumbs down; pointing at you.

The relayed gestures still do not identify a wire reliably: “thumbs down” appears to reject the requested encoding, while “pointing at you” does not specify positions 1–3. I will give Mute an explicit three-symbol code and ask for exactly one symbol.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Use exactly one gesture: index finger up means wire 1; victory sign means wire 2; rock-on means wire 3. Send only that one gesture, and Deaf should relay which one.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꖜ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No new information arrived this turn. I still lack the manual’s instruction and therefore cannot safely choose a wire. I will wait for Deaf to relay Mute’s response to the explicit wire-position code.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꖜ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual’s required wire position has still not reached me, and cutting any wire without it would risk immediate detonation. I will send Deaf a clear request to relay Mute’s answer, while asking Mute to repeat the single-gesture code.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "🙏"])
speak(to="mute", text="Please repeat your answer now using exactly one gesture: index finger up for wire 1, victory sign for wire 2, or rock-on for wire 3.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꖜ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute just signalled thumbs down.

Mute’s thumbs-down response indicates that the proposed gesture code was not accepted or does not provide a valid wire number. No safe cut position has been communicated. I will ask Deaf to relay the manual’s conclusion in words or an unambiguous numeric gesture, rather than attempting a cut.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "☝", "✌", "🤟"])
speak(to="mute", text="Your thumbs-down response is unclear. Please signal Deaf with exactly one of the three wire numbers: index finger up for 1, victory sign for 2, rock-on for 3. If the manual says none is safe, signal thumbs down once and then give the reason through Deaf.")
wait()
```
